title: Early gameplay from my mobile roguelite RPG
author: Cautious_Material_40
selftext:
Been working on this mobile roguelite RPG for about 2 weeks and wanted to share a quick battle clip!

I'm using Cursor for the coding, and I even had it build a custom animation editor directly into the game that lets me preview animations visually and fine-tune them instead of blindly asking AI to regenerate things over and over, which was wasting tokens.

I also found a workflow with ChatGPT that has made creating consistent sprite animations much faster.

The pixel art has a Final Fantasy Tactics-inspired look, but the gameplay is its own thing with different hero classes, unique skills and mechanics, boss fights, and short, 30-minute replayable runs.

It's still early, but I'd love to hear your first impressions.

Does the combat look satisfying? Is it easy to follow what's happening on screen? Does this look like something you'd play?

replies.author: Cautious_Material_40
replies.body:
Well, I started with chat gpt to try and generate the images, found it hard to have gpt produce animations without inconsistencies on the art. I  tried pixel lab, but the quality of the animations it made just looked too simple and basic.
I ended up refining how I get Chat GPT to create the images for me in workflow that makes it fairly easy to get new animations in the game.

replies.author: Long-Start-300
replies.body: Can you share how you got GPT to make better images for animations?

replies.author: Cautious_Material_40
replies.body:
I ended dup building a prompt that tells ai to build a 3x3 grid with 9 animations, grid needs to be evenly spaced, with the background color of my choosing so I can easily remove background in my process. I give it a style to replicate and the animation to create. Mostly works well but sometimes needs a helping hand follow up prompt.
I've found starting fresh chats help keep it on track and consistent.

comments.author: josh72811
comments.body: One thing I have been aiming for when making my game is to try to remove the AI "stench" so to speak. At least as much as possible. The few areas that stick out to me are the art form title screen, the background art of the battle screen, and the music. The music is the biggest offender for me. I think I hear four distinct songs play in the clip, the last one that plays is actually pretty good and blends in well (title screen too but it was very short). Game music is hard to get right because it has to feel good and forgettable at the same time. You don't really want the music to catch attention because then it distracts from the game. The music in the starting menu is very distracting. Then when the battle starts another song plays, and then it switches to another song... Lots of switches. I think annoying/overly distracting music can kill a game and often flies under the radar because people will dislike the game and not even know why.

replies.author: Cautious_Material_40
replies.body:
Thank you for checking this out and providing feedback!
So im actually a music artist myself, so music is a HUGE thing for me.
You are absolutely correct, you hear 4 different songs here, and I do think that's a lot in a 1 minute clip.
The title screen song, menu song, and 2 battle songs.
Id have to say, I absolutely want the music to standout in a way that makes the player feel a certain vibe.
-Title screen is basic enough.
-Menu screen im actually really in love with. This screen is visited frequently in game to buy skills and upgrades, so I wanted something that has a pretty relaxed feel but also contemplative. Its a short loop that keeps the energy going and let's the player think about what they want to upgrade.
-The 1st battle track is a special track reserved exclusively for the jester enemies. The jester enemies actually have special game mechanics and can reward toy or have devastating effects on the player, so the music is almost representative of a "boss". You dont really get that feeling because of how short the clip is A run takes about 30 minutes to complete)
-The 2nd battle song is just generic battle music that plays during battle.

Im definitely still adjusting how I want the music to feel in game and this feedback is definitely helpful.
Thanks for checking it out!

comments.author: cumbiaowl

replies.author: Cautious_Material_40
replies.body:
My mindset when building this was to make sure the Attack button is easy to use and ALWAYS useful, essentially being the core of the game for every class. A big attack button is easy to click, and it also gives you some useful information to use while fighting (got this idea from Final Fantasy Tactics).
With this in mind, ive built all of my systems around this mentality.
Attack and Guard are always reliable options so that it is easy to understand what you can do, while adding skills to compliment and further strategies. The ATTACK button builds the resources you need for those skills so its a core loop.

This was my thought process since the start, and hope I can stay consistent with this, since I think the gameplay loop is shaping up.

comments.author: stuffedcrust_studios
comments.body: it just looks too AI slopified in general, don't get me wrong I been using AI art tools myself but you gotta do something to give it it's own aesthetic and away from the default AI slop style. Many people will instantly switch off as soon as they see it and it gives it a 'cheap' feeling. I feel these days an aesthetic like this is akin to using times new roman font.

replies.author: Cautious_Material_40
replies.body:
Heard that!
Im not artist so I have to rely on what Ai produces for me.
I recognize that a lot of this looks like sloppy ai, but without a dedicated artist (and a bigger budget) im left to the ai gods to generate me usable artwork and animations.
Do you have any suggestions on how to improve the ai to give me better, more consistent, and less sloppy art?

replies.author: stuffedcrust_studios
replies.body:
i'm no artist either, but i think what's needed is to establish some kind aesthetic and vibe and try and get everything cohesive around that, also for me a trademark of AI UI design is it adds wayyy to much text and unecessary details everywhere and the screen just feels a bit cluttered and overloaded and with no clear visual hierarchy.   
  
Also things like font choices/sizes and general inconsistencies. It's really hard to pin down any one thing makes it look 'AI' it's kind of just an instant feel you get when you see it after having seen a lot of AI created stuff, maybe I am more sensitive than majority of players cos I been using these tools a lot though.

Here's a link to a post with a trailer I'm working on which is using mostly AI art right now - [https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1uyvn55/wip\_trailer\_for\_my\_pizza\_deckbuilder\_made\_using/](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1uyvn55/wip_trailer_for_my_pizza_deckbuilder_made_using/)

You may disagree and that's fine but I feel I've managed to craft some kind of aesthetic at least and mitigate that instant AI feel. Looking closely you can still find tells of course and I'm not trying to hide it, but just to not have that instant visceral 'this is pure unfiltered AI output therefore low effort therefore I'm not going to care about it' instinct that a lot of people have now developed.

I think the fact I'm building it Unity and am hand placing and arranging all the UI elements and choosing the colors etc contributes to that. If you let AI make too many choices the general AI feeling accumulates and it's harder to get rid of if that makes sense.
